To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The average occupation number is a function of momentum and temperature only; and 2) The grand partition function is the sum over the average occupation numbers.

(a) the average occupation number in momentum (wavevector) space,, is the appropriate quantity to use in order to formulate a variational principle that yields the grand partition function for a system of bosons (or fermions) interacting via a potential of arbitrary range, and (b) this variational principle is exact in the limit of a dilute gas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the theory of the BoseEinsten and FermiDirac gases.
a systematic investigation of the many-body problem in quantum statistical mechanics.

the development of a theory of many-particle systems in which the statistical character of the system (i.e. the nature of the distribution functions) is determined from a variational principle, and in which the thermodynamic properties are determined in a manner which is independent of the statistical character of each system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present paper represents the most complete and satisfactory formulation of the many-body problem in quantum statistical mechanics.
the author has developed a method for the solution of the many body problem in quantum statistics.
the author has developed a very powerful method for treating the many-body problem in the quantum statistics of a system of particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theory of quantum gases has been extended to the gaseous state, and the theory has been formulated in terms of a single variable, the average occupation number of a momentum state.

the present theory of the manybody problem is now sufficiently well developed to make it possible to calculate, in a systematic manner, the thermodynamic properties of a system of hard particles in the gaseoussolid transition region.
it provides a systematic method of calculating the thermodynamic properties of a system of particles with arbitrary interparticle potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of the quantum Boltzmann equation, the notion of the quantum state is a useful tool for the study of quantum transport in a wide variety of systems.
the use of the momentum space representation of the many-body wavefunction can be used to simplify the calculation of thermodynamic properties of quantum fluids.

the use of the momentum distribution as a variational parameter in the grand-canonical ensemble leads to a simple and systematic way to calculate the thermodynamic properties of interacting bosons near the BEC transition point.
